newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf shipping divided over state of Mina al-Bakr.
newsitem.headline: Gulf shipping divided over state of Mina al-Bakr.

text.p: Gulf shipping executives on Thursday were divided over the oil exporting capability of Iraq's Mina al-Bakr port ahead of expected United Nations approval to start partial exports.
A Dubai-based shipping executive said the port was in perfect order. "Mina al-Bakr is in fully operational condition. It has been for the last five months," he said.
"There has been trial pumping. They are also capable of ship to ship loading," he added.
Iraq oil ministry senior undersecretary Taha Hmud Mosa said on Tuesday Mina al-Bakr was capable of handling 1.2 million barrels per day (bpd).
He said Iraq intended to ship about 350,000 bpd via the Gulf port once the U.N. gives it the go-ahead under a partial export deal whose conditions Baghdad accepted on November 25.
The scheme, designed to ease the suffering of the Iraqi people under U.N. trade sanctions, allows Baghdad $2 billion of exports in six months.
Asked about Iraq's ability to handle 1.2 million bpd through Mina al-Bakr, a Gulf shipping source said: "I doubt it. It's an exaggeration."
Asked about Iraq's intended shipments of 350,000 bpd via the port, the source said: "That's more about it."
He said problems with a lack of spare parts and the fact that the port had been out of use for so long did not bode well for easy loading and shipping.

Another Dubai-based shipping source was confident Iraq would be able to ship 350,000 bpd through the port. "I think it is okay, but there is a lot of concern about the jetty -- if the physical structure of the jetty is alright."
Shipping sources said it was likely that Iraq was dredging the port daily of silt which flows into the sea through the delta.
